title: Filtered and Paged
description: A dispatcher narrows the tracking table down to just in-transit shipments, then pages through the results a few at a time. Confirm filtering and pagination compose correctly together rather than one silently overriding the other.
successCondition: Book 5 shipments and advance exactly 3 of them (as dispatcher/admin) into "in_transit" status (one tick from booked, stopping before delivered), leaving 2 as "booked". GET /api/tracking?status=in_transit&pageSize=2&page=1 as the dispatcher returns exactly 2 items, both with status "in_transit", and total equal to 3 (or more, if the environment has other in_transit shipments, but at least 3 including yours). GET /api/tracking?status=in_transit&pageSize=2&page=2 returns the remaining in_transit item(s), with no overlap in shipment ids between the two pages.
hints: One call to POST /api/tracking/:id/advance moves a shipment from booked to in_transit — a second call would move it further, so stop at exactly one tick for the 3 you want to remain in_transit.
Cross-check the shipment ids returned across page 1 and page 2 against your known set of 5 to confirm no shipment appears on both pages or is missing from both.
